Playbook.name: Windows — DPAPI Master Key Backup Retrieved from a New Host - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A DPAPI domain backup key was retrieved (4692) from a host not seen doing this before (new_terms). Attackers retrieve the DPAPI backup key to decrypt any user's protected secrets domain-wide. Triage question: legitimate backup/credential operation, or DPAPI backdoor abuse?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: The DPAPI domain backup key decrypts every domain user's DPAPI-protected secrets (browser passwords, saved credentials) - a master skeleton key.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host that retrieved the backup key.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the DPAPI backup-key retrieval is a legitimate operation or credential-theft abuse from an unexpected host.

Step.name: Who retrieved the DPAPI key and from where
Step.Purpose: Legitimate retrieval comes from known credential-management infrastructure; a workstation/unexpected host is the finding.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4692" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.MasterKeyId | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: An interactive user or an endpoint retrieving the DPAPI backup key is abnormal; legitimate use is rare and tied to specific admin operations. new_terms fired because this host is first-seen for it.

Step.name: What else is this principal/host doing (credential-theft context)
Step.Purpose: DPAPI abuse usually sits in a credential-theft chain (LSASS access, mimikatz, mass secret decryption).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4672","4688","4624") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Privileged logon/process activity around the retrieval supports an attack chain; a quiet host with a documented admin operation supports benign.

Node.Condition: An endpoint/workstation or unfamiliar principal retrieved the DPAPI backup key, especially amid other credential activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (DPAPI Backdoor Abuse - IR immediately)

Node.Condition: Retrieval by a documented credential-management/backup operation from expected infrastructure.
Retrieval from a server whose role for this operation is unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-DPAPI-WHO, INV-02-DPAPI-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the operation; baseline the host; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Abuse of the DPAPI backup key to decrypt domain secrets.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; open IR; treat all DPAPI-protected secrets as exposed.
Consider DPAPI backup key rotation; reset widely-exposed credentials.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A backup tool mis-scoped to retrieve the key.

Indicators.Item: A backup service doing so unexpectedly.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
